title: Formal system
summary: A declared language together with axioms and inference rules used to determine which expressions count as derivable.

context.note: This is a schematic metalogical description; particular formal systems require their own exact records.

content.plain: A formal system fixes the symbols you may write, the starting statements you accept, and the rules by which new statements may be derived.
content.exact: For QEVA seed purposes, a formal system S is specified by at least a formal language L, a designated set or scheme of axioms A, and inference rules R. A complete record must also state any syntax and proof conventions required to determine valid derivations.
content.example: A presentation of propositional logic may specify formulas, axiom schemes, and modus ponens.
content.caveat: Different foundations package syntax, axioms, rules, semantics, and definitions differently; QEVA must record the chosen presentation rather than force one universal encoding.

relations.note: Derivability is defined only after a proof system is fixed.

verification.method: QEVA seed formulation checked editorially for mathematical coherence; no external formal proof artifact is claimed.

provenance.creator: QEVA seed archive
provenance.source_note: Seed record written to make QEVA Protocol 0.2 explicit. It is an editorial mathematical formulation, not a claim that one foundation is uniquely privileged.
